balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): total revenue has been roughly flat since FY2021 (RMB575m to RMB904m FY2025) because a shrinking finance (lending) line is being offset by a fast-growing services (platform fee) line -- see the Revenue Mix chart below for the underlying shift.

What to watch:

  • Whether total growth re-accelerates once the lending book stops shrinking
  • Interim rows show seasonality

revenueMix.title: Revenue mix: finance vs services
revenueMix.content:
Finance revenue is interest and fee income earned on the supply-chain financing book SY Holdings holds or facilitates. Services revenue is fees earned from the asset-light digital/technology platform -- data, risk-management and transaction-processing services sold to banks and other financiers without SY Holdings taking the credit exposure itself.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): this is the central story of the business. Finance revenue peaked in FY2023 (RMB722.8m) and has fallen since (RMB375.9m FY2025) as the group deliberately shrinks its own balance-sheet lending. Services revenue has grown almost every period, from RMB50.2m in FY2021 to RMB473.5m in FY2025, and overtook finance revenue for the first time in FY2025. The pivot is from a capital-intensive, credit-risk-bearing lender to a fee-based platform operator -- the name change from Sheng Ye Capital to SY Holdings Group reflects it.

What to watch:

  • Whether services revenue growth keeps outpacing the finance-revenue decline so total revenue inflects upward
  • Services revenue is higher-margin and does not carry credit risk, so the mix shift should lift blended margins and lower capital intensity over time
  • A renewed increase in finance revenue would signal the group re-levering its own balance sheet rather than continuing the asset-light pivot

associatesProfit.title: Share of associates' profit
associatesProfit.content:
Share of associates' profit is SY Holdings' equity-accounted share of net income from businesses it holds a minority, non-controlling stake in (joint ventures and associates), rather than revenue it bills directly.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): this line has grown from roughly RMB17m in FY2021 to RMB151.3m in FY2025 and is now a meaningful contributor to net income, reflecting the group's strategy of partnering into financing platforms and data ventures rather than owning the credit risk outright -- the same asset-light logic as the services-revenue pivot.

What to watch:

  • Whether this income is cash-backed (dividends received) or purely accounting recognition
  • Concentration risk if one or two associates drive most of the gain
  • Consistency of growth versus one-off associate disposals or revaluations

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For SY Holdings Group Limited (formerly Sheng Ye Capital Limited): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
